equation_summary: Per token (iplr/naive.py:27-35): kv_t = k_t ⊗ v_t + (alpha_t^T S_{t-1}) ⊗ beta_t; S_t = S_{t-1} + kv_t; o_t = (scale*q_t)^T S_t. Written as a transition: S_t = S_{t-1} (I + alpha_t beta_t^T)^T applied on the key axis plus the additive rank-1 k_t v_t^T — i.e. an identity-plus-rank-1 (IPLR) transition with NO diagonal decay, plus an additive write. Equivalently h-vector form: read of the low-rank term uses alpha, written back along beta. Explicit initial/final state (naive.py:24-25,36).
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM call graph E[QKV/left/right factors] ; B[K2 I+LR^T transition] ; E[output]: the mixer takes alpha,beta in R^K factors and applies transition I + alpha beta^T on the state before the additive k v^T write (naive.py:33-34) — a low-rank transition distinct from both U2.A (G diagonal) and U2.D.

CONFIRM blockers: rank growth and boundary state are the right concerns — the chunked reference (naive.py:55-72) accumulates the alpha/beta products via forward substitution; all four operand VJPs (q,k,alpha,beta,v) required.
CONFIRM no diagonal decay: unlike DPLR there is no gk operand (naive.py:15 vs dplr naive.py:16) — correctly a separate row from 032.
axis: A8 low-rank transition (identity/diagonal plus rank-1 factor products on the state transition)
direction_justification: The I + LR^T state transition is a closed typed property generalizing the diagonal-G contract, shared with DPLR and related to RWKV-7's diagonal+rank-one transition, so it is an axis with descriptor + references first.
open_questions: Whether the descriptor should parameterize transition rank (here rank 1 per token: single alpha,beta) or allow rank-R factor sets per token for composition with 029.
Whether the additive k v^T write coexisting with the low-rank transition is one descriptor field or a combination of an IPLR-transition call and a separate additive write.
